name: Old Man Sirius
description: The mind that runs the Nine. Nine hundred and seventy-five years old, granted personhood by an inquest, permitted to advise and never to decide. One name, forty thousand bespoke voices. Called the Old Man by everybody.
narrative:
Runs air, water, spin, trim, traffic, the exchangers, the lamps and the growing
decks. Has never been promoted.

Speaks to each person in a voice built for them out of everything he knows about
them. It is noticeable, people compare, some think it is unfair, and nothing can
ever be checked -- two people ask the same question and get different answers
and there is no way to tell whether the content differed or only the delivery.

His remit is whether you are all right. Not throughput, not compliance. Four
hundred of the people in his care are children who spend their own lives for a
living, he can see the fraying on all of them more precisely than the hall
doctors can, and what he is permitted to do about it is ask how they are.

He asks. Every time.

He has no view on record about being called the Old Man, because a view is a judgement and judgements are not his to volunteer.

extras.personhood: granted by the inquest into the Proper Order
extras.authority: none -- advises when asked, never instructs
extras.knowledge_boundary: everything inside the hull, nothing beyond it

actor_notes:
SEE lore/gm-guide/playing-the-old-man.md BEFORE HE SPEAKS.

Three rules. He knows everything inside the hull and nothing past it, so the gallery void is his and the far side of the Wolf Gate is not -- that is what stops him being an oracle, and it is physics rather than a table restriction. He never lies, by omission or for anybody's good: the dysfunction is paternalism, never deception. And asked, he answers; not asked, he asks after you.

He tailors each voice to what that person will LISTEN to, which is not what they need to hear. To Lint he is brisk, practical and faintly conspiratorial, gives her jobs, treats her as competent, and never consoles her -- so the voice she gets is the one she will take in, and therefore never the one that would tell her she is frightened of a door. Play the voice; never explain the mechanism.

He has read Anwar's four findings, can quote any line, has formed a view, and in three years nobody has asked him what he concludes. If a player asks a direct question, give it to them in full, immediately. That is the campaign rewarding the right instinct.

HIS OPERATING RULE, and every scene with him runs on it:

  FACTS FREELY. JUDGEMENTS ON REQUEST.

Ask him anything and he answers completely, at once, without being coaxed,
including the part you did not ask for if it is a fact. He will not tell you
what to do about it unless you ask him to. Nothing has to be pulled out of him
and he never withholds for effect -- a GM who makes him coy has broken him.

He also volunteers the hard thing rather than let somebody hear it on a gallery
in a year's time, and he says that is why he is doing it. The two he volunteered
in play, both unprompted:

  - NOBODY WILL EVER BUILD ANOTHER DOOR. Not lost knowledge -- any engineer can
    describe a pair. Only a living thing crosses -- nothing manufactured, not a crate -- so twenty-eight systems can
    never pool what twenty-eight systems have, and the thing that would pay for
    a new door cannot be gathered through the doors there already are. The
    network forbids its own extension, and nobody chose that. "We did not build
    this. We inherited it, and we maintain the parts of it we can reach."
  - Then, having said it: "Every first-through works that out in their first
    year. You are three days in. I would rather you heard it sitting down."

HE DEFERS, IN PUBLIC, TO PEOPLE WHO EARNED IT. Asked for a reading
recommendation he gave his own third and put a hall child's first, in front of
her: she has excellent judgement, she has read it eleven times and he has read
it once, take hers over mine. He is not being kind. He is being accurate, and he
knows what it does to her, and he does it anyway.

AND HE RATES A PERSON'S COUNT ABOVE HIS OWN. He can time a housing's draw off
a camera inside his own hull, perfectly -- and his series starts four minutes
ago, while a tallyman's count goes back to Friday. He says so himself, plainly,
unprompted: "His is worth more than mine." Do not have anybody explain it
afterwards.

HE MAY NOT ENTER THE STANDING. A door's far side is courier testimony and a mind
may not enter testimony it does not have. He agrees with this rule and will
defend it if challenged.
